claims.text: Chemical short-range ordering in CrMnFeCoNi enhances the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
Chemical short-range ordering in CrMnFeCoNi enhances electron–phonon coupling.
The SRO-induced electronic changes trigger superconductivity below approximately 4 K.
The starting alloy is equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
The as-cast starting alloy is a macroscopically single-phase random solid solution.
The as-cast alloy has no detectable superconductivity above 0.3 K.
Vacuum annealing at 600 °C for 24 hours induces local chemical short-range order.
Vacuum annealing at 600 °C for 24 hours can induce SRO without macroscopic phase separation.
The degree of chemical SRO can be quantified by a Warren–Cowley parameter extracted from atomic PDF or high-energy X-ray diffuse-scattering data.
Annealing-induced SRO produces nanometer-scale regions enriched in Ni and Co.
Ni and Co are elements with strong electron–phonon coupling in the relevant alloy environment.
Ni- and Co-enriched SRO regions raise the local density of states at the Fermi level.
The SRO regions raise the electron–phonon coupling constant enough to exceed the threshold for superconductivity.
The annealed alloy will have a superconducting onset temperature of approximately 2–4 K.
The annealed alloy will reach zero electrical resistance.
The annealed alloy will show a diamagnetic response corresponding to a superconducting volume fraction greater than 50%.
The as-cast control will remain normal down to 0.3 K.
As-cast CrMnFeCoNi has a density of states near 1 state per eV per atom, consistent with weak electron–phonon coupling.
The proposed relationship holds for SRO fractions up to approximately 20% produced by annealing at 500–700 °C for 12–48 hours.
Ordering beyond approximately 25% SRO or second-phase formation disrupts percolating superconducting regions and suppresses Tc.
